Dakota

By: Paul Nel | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Flying enthusiasts bid farewell to an iconic vintage aircraft, as it leaves Africa for its new home in Europe.

Summary:
Our feature focusses on a vintage Dakota aircraft which has traversed the continent for decades - first as a military plane - and then as a luxuary flying safari aircraft, owned and operated by Capt. Flippie Vermeulen - a former SAA Captain, and the man who started flying safaris in Africa. Now retired after an epic journey up the Great African Rift Valley - Dakota NTE flies to her new home in Luxemburg - where she will entertain flying enthusiasts from across Europe. We join her on this epic journey across the Mediteranean and on to Europe.

We will be interviewing the following people:

1. Flippie Vermeulen - Owner of Springbok Flying safaris - 0118242142
2. Maryna Vermeuelen - Co-owner and wife of Flippie Vermeulen - 0118242142
3. Capt. Noel Flynn & Capt. Ulrich Spielman - Cargolux Captains and stand-by captains on journey - noel.flynn@cargolux.com
4. Harrald Scheppig - German hotelier and co-founder of african sfafri excursions - International contact details to be supplied asap.

Web Contacts:
www.springboksafaris.com

Locations:
SA to Europe

Press Release:


Dakota’s African Epic
13000 Dakota DC3 aircraft were produced in 1933, exactly 33 years after the Wright brothers made history by taking the first powered flight. In recent years one of these vintage Dakotas has taken well-heeled clientele on luxury safaris across Africa from the Great Rift Valley to the Serengeti. Now, this spectacular airplane has been sold to a wealthy German. Carte Blanche joins her owner and pilot Captain Flippie Vermeulen in an 11 day excursion across West Africa and the Mediterranean and on to her new home in Europe.


Script:


CB Dakota Script.
PGM:
The year was 1957 and young Flippie Vermeulen dreamed of flying. It was all he could think about. Lying in the veld he saw a plane flying overhead. It was a Douglas DC3, one of the world’s most iconic aircraft. Instinctively, Flippie knew that he would fly the prop liner.
INT: FLIPPIE:
‘My association with the Dc3 started when I was nineteen years old, when I was trained onto Dc3’s in the air Force – so I’ve always had this interest in old-timer prop-liner airplanes’.
PGM:
After serving in the Air force, a career in SAA followed, and Capt Vermeulen became instrumental in founding the historical flight division using Junkers, JU52, DC4’s and DC6’s. Flying passengers in the aircraft was a rewarding experience, but the ultimate prize was piloting the DC3 Dakota across Africa – and overseas.
Under Flippie’s guidance, historical flights evolved into a highly popular and gratifying form of flying adventures, that could only be described as ‘Classic Flying Safaris’- complete with wild elephants having to be chased off the runway prior to landing. This was the Africa depicted in early Hollywood movies.
INT FLIPPIE: ‘And I then decided to use my expertise which I gained over a twelve year period with the old aeroplanes – and I started the family business in 2001, which we then called, ‘Springbok Flying Safaris’, which is essentially exactly what it says. Flying safaris with old timer aeroplanes.
PGM: Flippie acquired his second Dakota ZS-NTE and completely restored it.
INT: FLIPPIE:
‘The viability of these old aero planes alone is extremely difficult and we knew we had to find a way to continue our operation – and what we did – we developed the all inclusive package tours concept’.
PGM:
The package tours resulted in wealthy European clients flying as far north as the Serengeti in Tanzania, where they could witness the famous migration of wildlife.
The further they travelled however, meant an increasing risk for the DC3 should repairs be required. Fuel was always in short supply – and long hours were spent pumping hundreds of gallons buy hand.
As an aging pilot flying an aging aircraft, Flippie made the painful decision to sell his beloved DC3. The era of grand air safaris had come to an end.
INT: FLIPPIE:
And it was – in my opinion, one of the last great big air safaris with vintage planes’.
And so… on a perfect Highveld winter’s morning in May, Flippie and his crew boarded NTE and prepared to embark on an eleven Odyssey up the West Coast of Africa – across the Atlantic on onwards to Europe, to her new home in Germany.

In the early 1900s the Wright brothers awakened the sense of wonder in those eager to experience the excitement and adventure of powered flight. Thirty three years later the first of over 13000 DC3s rolled of the assembly line in America. It was the dawn of luxury passenger prop liners. Well heeled enthusiast quaffed champagne and dined on canapé’s, unaware that war loomed on the horizon.
Douglas’ DC3evloved into the C47 cargo transporter – becoming legend for its remarkable logistic capabilities. British high command christened her Dakota and the aircraft was extensively used to ferry paratroopers, whilst being instrumental in the Berlin airlift. Dakota had made her mark.
A post-war surplus of the battle tested c47 resulted in the airplane being utilized by air forces across the globe – including here at home where she was dubbed the ‘Vomit Comet’. Flippie’s dream of flying the DC3 became reality.
Lowering the right wing – NTE bade South Africa farewell.
Conflicts in East African countries negated flying a shorter route up the Rift Valley – and the pilots set course for Namibia – and up the Skeleton Coast burning 400 liters of fuel per hour, and providing 1200hp, NTE slowly flew up the coast to the Central African Republic, Gabon, Ghana, Mali and finally onto Dakar in Senegal.
Captain Ulrich Spielman had never flown at low level in Africa. It was a unique experience.
INT: ULI:
‘When do you get a chance to ferry a prop liner – to be specific, a vintage prop liner
The Atlantic crossing endured for a grueling 6 hours – only a few hundred meters above the sea.
INT:
Landing in The Grand Canary Islands’, Las Palmas - brought back memories for Flippie.
INT:
Crew members enjoyed a brief stopover – and before long the were airborne on a 7 hour leg past the straights of Gibraltar and onto Cascais in Portugal.
NTE’s unpressurised and unheated cabin become chilly, but pilot spirits were bolstered when the Portuguese coastline came into view.
A local aviation club turned out in numbers to welcome NTE and her crew to Europe – all were eager to take in as much information about the flight as possible. They’d been tracking the journey via Internet.
This was to be the penultimate stop before reaching Zweibrucken. Fuel had to be taken on board and crew members were eager to spruce up the aircraft for her new owner.
An early evening in downtown Cascais ended a very long day.
Daybreak. This final leg of the journey would be the longest at just over nine hours. NTE departed Cascais for a routing over Spain and then France towards Germany. Finally, after 11 days and against almost insurmountable odds, Zweibrucken airport loomed into view and Captain Spielman landed NTE.
INT:
Peter Adrian, NTE’s new owner reappeared the next morning flying his classic Beech 18. He was eager to meet with Flippie again and to view his new acquisition. NTE had been purchased to bolster Peter’s classic aircraft collection including this beautiful Steerman. Flippie was informed that Peter had also purchased Zweibrucken Airport, a former NATO airbase – and that the DC3 had pride of place in a very exclusive hangar.
The epic ferry flight was over.

10” Teaser Promo One voice:

Classic flying safaris on the continent originated right here in South Africa – thanks to one man’s vision, and a trusted vintage prop liner fondly known as, ‘The Vomit Comet’.

10” Teaser Promo Two voice:
“An iconic vintage Dakota used by the South African Air Force, as well as privately for classic air safaris – is flown to Europe during an epic eleven day journey, after being sold”

Alternatives:

“Join us for an incredible eleven day adventure flying the famous DC 3 Dakota up the west coast of Africa – to her new home in Germany”

“Join us as we experience unforgettable classic air safaris aboard an iconic DC 3 Dakota – before the airplane is flown to a new home in Germany”.
